## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

```diff

-    "downloads",
     "declarativeNetRequest",
+    "downloads",

=== index 12
💡 **SUGGESTION: the download size cap is pre-check-only — enforce it in the settle loop too**

The 256 MiB cap is enforced only in `_probeDownloadSize` (HEAD → Content-Length). Two uncapped windows remain:

1. **Unknown length**: chunked responses and opaque (no-cors) responses return `null` → `size_precheck: "unknown"` → an arbitrarily large download proceeds. The code comments are honest about this ("the cap then stays best-effort"), but F2′ sells the tool as "size-capped".
2. **After the wait returns**: `_awaitDownloadSettled` gives up after 10 s and reports `in_progress` — the download keeps running with no cap ever re-checked.

Both close with the polling loop you already have: inside `_awaitDownloadSettled`, when `item.fileSize > defaultMaxDownloadBytes`, `await _chrome.downloads.cancel(id)` and surface `download_too_large` instead of the in-progress note. That converts the cap from advisory to enforced for every case where the item is observable, at the cost of one comparison per 250 ms poll.

Also worth one line in the tool description: "size-capped" currently reads as a guarantee; say it is a Content-Length pre-check plus in-flight enforcement, with unknown-length downloads capped only by the in-flight check.

Minor docstring nit in the same area: `DownloadItem.fileSize` in `chrome_api.dart` is commented "Bytes received so far" — Chrome's `fileSize` is the expected total size (`bytesReceived` is the received-so-far counter). The mapping reads the right field; only the comment misleads.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

## Permission⇄tool matrix

`permission_matrix.dart` is ONE declarative table answering "which
chrome permission backs which tool, at which tier" — the single source
of truth the manifest, the tool registry and the docs derive from. A
two-way checker (`checkMatrix`) turns every drift into a typed
`MatrixViolation` (`dead_permission`, `ghost_tool`, `exposed_excluded`,
`tier_mismatch`) instead of a silent gap.

| Tier | Rows | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Core** | 41 — the 27 curated-tool roots (incl. `runtime`, which needs no permission) + 12 bridge-only roots (`search`, `readingList`, `tabCapture`, `browsingData`, `tts`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `privacy`, `proxy`, `management`, `clipboard`, `nativeMessaging`, `webRequest`) + `browser_api` + `browser_api_catalog` themselves | Registered and exposed; an unpacked manifest must carry the permission |
| **Second tier** | 3 (`topSites`, `pageCapture`, `userScripts`) | Implemented but registered-hidden — a Settings gate turns them on; permissions ride `optional_permissions` |
| **Excluded (gh-1630)** | `identity`, `contentSettings`, `fontSettings`, `desktopCapture` | CWS Purple Potassium: requested-but-unused is a hard rejection — removed with the tools/rows that backed them; re-add only WITH shipping code. `downloads` is the F2′ exception: RETAINED, with the gated `download` tool as its shipped call site |
| **Excluded** | 12 (`gcm`, `instanceID`, `devtools`, `fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`, `printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`, `enterprise.deviceAttributes`, `enterprise.networkingAttributes`, `passwords`) | Absent from manifest AND registry; the table row records the rationale so absence is auditable |

Issue #137 moved `browsingData`/`tts`/`declarativeNetRequest`/`privacy`/
`proxy`/`management` (and the Tier-1 additions above) from excluded or
optional into **core + declared**: the manifest now carries the maximum
viable permission set and the bridge exposes each declared namespace —
permissions without access are pure waste. `management` is declared but
the bridge DENIES `chrome.management` calls in every mode
(self-preservation; the row exists so the permission is auditable).
Remaining excluded rationales: `gcm`/`instanceID` are push transport,
not an agent surface; `devtools` opens interactive windows; the
ChromeOS-only set (`fileBrowserHandler`, `printing`,
`printingMetrics`, `fileSystemProvider`, `platformKeys`, `wallpaper`)
and the `enterprise.*` pair (device-admin) have no desktop-agent

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.

                fail(f"{name}: checksum mismatch — on disk {got}, lock pins "
                     f"{want}. The staged vendor tree is stale or tampered.")
            # Drifted bytes: the on-disk payload is untrusted (E1), so it
            # is deleted and the file is re-fetched from the lock URL —
            # the log line must describe what actually happens, and the
            # only verify() that matters runs on the fresh download below.
            print(f"vendor: {name} differs from the lock — re-fetching")
            os.remove(out_path)
        elif verify_only:
            fail(f"{name}: missing from {dest} and --verify-only skips "
                 "network — run the full fetch first")
        if verify_only:
            continue
        if not os.path.exists(out_path):
            print(f"vendor: downloading {name} ({engine} {version})")
        tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        # -fsSL: fail on HTTP errors, follow redirects, silent; retries
        # for the flaky big-wasm legs. --retry-max-time spans CDN
        # rate-limit windows (jsdelivr 503s arrive in bursts — 4×3s
        # exhausted them and failed the whole build, gh-1630): 6 tries
        # spread over up to 5 min ride out a window per file.
        subprocess.run(
            ["curl", "-fsSL", "--retry", "6", "--retry-delay", "5",
             "--retry-max-time", "300", "--retry-all-errors",
             url, "-o", tmp],
            check=True,
        )
        data = open(tmp, "rb").read()
        data = verify(data)
        # Ship the VERIFIED (replacement-transformed) bytes: verify()
        # transforms in memory, tmp still holds the raw download —
        # renaming it straight over the destination shipped the raw
        # upstream payload and the packaging guard rejected the zip
        # (remote-code markers the lock replacements had already
        # stripped in memory). Overwrite tmp, then atomically rename.
        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(tmp, out_path)
        fetched += 1
        print(f"vendor: {name} fetched + verified "
              f"({len(data)} bytes)")","path":"scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"}

content.text:
`cd flutter_agent_harness/flutter_app && flutter run`.

## Chrome extension

- MV3 extension that hosts the full Fa web app in a side panel; the agent
  runs in the service worker and drives the browser with 34 tools:
  `tabs_open`, `tabs_close`, `tabs_update`, `tabs_query`, `tabs_move`,
  `tabs_group`, `tabs_ungroup`, `tabs_reload`, `tabs_discard`,
  `windows_open`, `windows_update`, `windows_close`, `windows_list`,
  `groups_update`, `groups_close`, `sessions_recent`, `sessions_restore`,
  `history_search`, `bookmarks_list`, `bookmarks_add`, `bookmarks_update`,
  `bookmarks_remove`, `downloads_start`, `downloads_search`,
  `downloads_cancel`, `cookies_get`, `cookies_set`, `cookies_remove`,
  `inject_js`, `inject_css`, `cdp_eval`, `page_screenshot`,
  `app_screenshot`, `nav_wait` — plus four Settings-gated second-tier
  tools that surface once the user enables them:
===
  git clone/push over HTTP and SSH, python3 with pip, sqlite3, QuickJS, file
  edits, web search/fetch, subagents, LSP, MCP tools, persistent memory,
  checkpoint/rewind, and long sessions with automatic context compaction;
  the Chrome extension adds 34 browser tools, Outlook adds three mail tools.
- Is it free? The project is MIT-licensed open source; users pay their own LLM
  provider for tokens only — no subscription or account.
- How to install the CLI? `curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh`

  tools that surface once the user enables them:
===
  git clone/push over HTTP and SSH, python3 with pip, sqlite3, QuickJS, file
  edits, web search/fetch, subagents, LSP, MCP tools, persistent memory,
  checkpoint/rewind, and long sessions with automatic context compaction;
  the Chrome extension adds 34 browser tools, Outlook adds three mail tools.
- Is it free? The project is MIT-licensed open source; users pay their own LLM
  provider for tokens only — no subscription or account.
- How to install the CLI? `curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh`

  `tabs_open`, `tabs_close`, `tabs_update`, `tabs_query`, `tabs_move`,
  `tabs_group`, `tabs_ungroup`, `tabs_reload`, `tabs_discard`,
  `windows_open`, `windows_update`, `windows_close`, `windows_list`,
  `groups_update`, `groups_close`, `sessions_recent`, `sessions_restore`,
  `history_search`, `bookmarks_list`, `bookmarks_add`, `bookmarks_update`,
  `bookmarks_remove`, `downloads_start`, `downloads_search`,
  `downloads_cancel`, `cookies_get`, `cookies_set`, `cookies_remove`,
  `inject_js`, `inject_css`, `cdp_eval`, `page_screenshot`,
  `app_screenshot`, `nav_wait` — plus four Settings-gated second-tier
  tools that surface once the user enables them:
===
  git clone/push over HTTP and SSH, python3 with pip, sqlite3, QuickJS, file
  edits, web search/fetch, subagents, LSP, MCP tools, persistent memory,
  checkpoint/rewind, and long sessions with automatic context compaction;
  the Chrome extension adds 34 browser tools, Outlook adds three mail tools.
- Is it free? The project is MIT-licensed open source; users pay their own LLM
  provider for tokens only — no subscription or account.
- How to install the CLI? `curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh`

Tool error (bash): #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).
# Without dart: a previously built sw/agent.js ships if present, else the
# zip is scaffold-only with a warning (never a failure).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs zip + python3|node|grep.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

with_app=0
case "${1:-}" in
  --with-app) with_app=1 ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $1 (usage: $0 [--with-app])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

manifest=browser_ext/manifest.json

# The manifest carries // comments (Chrome's parser is lenient, strict
# JSON validators are not) — strip them before validating, the same
# regex test/browser_ext/chrome_driver.dart uses.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
' "$manifest"
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, ""))' "$manifest"
else
  grep -q '"manifest_version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*3' "$manifest"
fi

# --- Vendored engine assets (gh-1630 I2): fetched ONLY from
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json, SHA-256-verified, fail-loud on mismatch.
# Covers the offscreen run_script runtimes AND the panel app's on-device

content.text:
Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.
- `scripts/check_cws_compliance.py` (new) + `ext_package_guard.py` remote
  scan: AC1 byte-scan of sources AND the built zip, manifest/privacy/lock
  asserts — wired into `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml`, red blocks
  merge (REG-1).

### Test Coverage

- `test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart` (8), `test/site/privacy_policy_test.dart` (4),
  `flutter_app/test/web_interpreters_urls_test.dart` (3) — new; the
  compliance tests failed before the fix, pass after.
- Full suites: root dart 10,982 passed / 0 failed; browser_ext/dart 451;
  node 46; Playwright run-script (vendored quickjs + pyodide in the real
  extension) 6/6; panel-app e2e 2 passed (real app renders, no fatal
  overlay).
- Artifact: `build/fa-extension.zip` (155 entries) passes the packaging
  guard — byte-scan finds zero remote-code markers in the package;
  compiled `main.dart.js`: 0 jsdelivr, 5 `vendor/interpreters` paths.
- Panel console checker (jsdelivr allowlist removed — any CDN mention is
  now fatal): `fatal=0 consoleErrors=0` in real headless Chrome.

### Notes

- The extension's CSP keeps blocking every remote host; `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`
  is the Google-recommended scoped exception the vendored wasm engines
  need (pyodide/onnxruntime/quickjs) — it does not re-enable `eval`.
- The hosted web app and Office taskpane keep loading engines from CDNs
  (unchanged behavior, tree-shaken out of the extension build).

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.
- `scripts/check_cws_compliance.py` (new) + `ext_package_guard.py` remote
  scan: AC1 byte-scan of sources AND the built zip, manifest/privacy/lock
  asserts — wired into `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml`, red blocks
  merge (REG-1).

### Test Coverage

- `test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart` (8), `test/site/privacy_policy_test.dart` (4),
  `flutter_app/test/web_interpreters_urls_test.dart` (3) — new; the
  compliance tests failed before the fix, pass after.
- Full suites: root dart 10,982 passed / 0 failed; browser_ext/dart 451;
  node 46; Playwright run-script (vendored quickjs + pyodide in the real
  extension) 6/6; panel-app e2e 2 passed (real app renders, no fatal
  overlay).
- Artifact: `build/fa-extension.zip` (155 entries) passes the packaging
  guard — byte-scan finds zero remote-code markers in the package;
  compiled `main.dart.js`: 0 jsdelivr, 5 `vendor/interpreters` paths.
- Panel console checker (jsdelivr allowlist removed — any CDN mention is
  now fatal): `fatal=0 consoleErrors=0` in real headless Chrome.

### Notes

- The extension's CSP keeps blocking every remote host; `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`
  is the Google-recommended scoped exception the vendored wasm engines
  need (pyodide/onnxruntime/quickjs) — it does not re-enable `eval`.
- The hosted web app and Office taskpane keep loading engines from CDNs
  (unchanged behavior, tree-shaken out of the extension build).
